data.narrative:
Orchid is a Series A biotech company founded by Noor Siddiqui that has raised $16.5M to date. The valuation universe comprises three public comparables (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and eight private peers in Biotech & Health, including Colossal Biosciences, Abridge, and Chai Discovery. However, the private peer set lacks sufficient clustering around the same stage and valuation tier to support meaningful median benchmarking.

Stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable valuation approach. Using total raised ($16.5M) as a proxy for current value and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement yields an implied valuation of $33M. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples is not feasible; while the three public biotech comparables trade at a median 6.6x price-to-sales, Orchid's revenue is not on file, preventing multiple application. Peer-median analysis was excluded due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the target valuation tier.

The triangulation analysis, constrained to a single applicable method, supports a range of $28M (low) to $38M (high), with $33M as the median point estimate. Key uncertainties include the limited methodological foundation—reliance on stage-progression alone—and the absence of disclosed financial metrics that would enable revenue or profitability-based valuation. The narrow peer set also limits confidence in the 2.0x multiplier assumption for this particular company.
